solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fancy pigeon losing head in the course of occasion for herd

indicators.note: losing its head means the pigeon word gives up its opening letter
something happening in the course of an event sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an hour is a set time or occasion, as in 'the hour has come'
a barb is a fancy breed of domestic pigeon; without its first letter it becomes ARB

explanation.surface: A pigeon fancier's bird goes missing at the moment the cattle are being gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the bird's description: a fancy pigeon is one bred for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives herd as a verb meaning to shelter or keep safe, the same sense as giving someone or something refuge.

clue.text: Hospital march is upsetting — that’s settled

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns a word upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A protest march past a hospital causes distress, but the matter is then resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something homed has been given a home, so it is settled in a fixed place.

clue.text: Bears no longer pray to get into rising tide

indicators.note: to get into something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another
in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: the sea, the body of water that ebbs and flows; as it rises it reads AES
bid is an obsolete word meaning to pray or beg, hence 'no longer'

explanation.surface: Bears that have given up praying wade into an incoming tide.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA reversed is AES, and BID goes inside it after the A. 'no longer' marks an archaic sense, a convention in barred puzzles like the Mephisto.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate or put up with it, which is to bear it.

clue.text: False god is flat out of name

indicators.note: out of name here means without the letter standing for name, which is dropped

blocks.note: flat in the sense of dull and uninspired
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An idol turns out to be dull and has lost its reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking N from BANAL leaves BAAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Baal was a Canaanite deity denounced in the Old Testament, so the name stands for any idol or false object of worship.

clue.text: Ordinary gel one picked up for roustabout’s place of work

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted from bottom to top, so the letters run upwards

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary
gel is a jocular upper-class pronunciation of girl, listed as a word in its own right
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ordinary young woman is collected and taken to an oilfield worker's site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gel' suggests hair product, but it is the posh way of saying girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A roustabout is an unskilled labourer on an offshore drilling platform, so the platform is where such a worker is employed.

clue.text: Secret unit, if denied freely

indicators.note: freely means without constraint, so the letters are free to fall into any order

blocks.note: the letters of the three words taken together

explanation.surface: A covert military unit's existence is readily denied by the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unidentified has not been named or revealed, so its identity is kept hidden or unknown.

clue.text: Just specified as aristocracy curbing good access

indicators.note: curbing means restraining or cutting back, so the aristocracy word is cut back by losing a letter

blocks.note: just in the sense of fair and correct
of introduces what something is specified as, as in 'the city of York'
the gentry are the landed upper class
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A statement that the upper classes are being restrained from good access.
explanation.definitionFit: A right of entry is a legal entitlement to go into a property, so it is a form of permitted admission.

clue.text: Feature restaurant embracing Italy

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature on a restaurant that showcases Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic or quality, which is what a feature of a person or thing is.

clue.text: Work involving not specified tissue

indicators.note: involving means including within, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: toil is hard work
n.s. is the abbreviation for not specified

explanation.surface: A job that involves some unspecified tissue, perhaps in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Each tonsil is a mass of lymphoid tissue at the back of the throat.

clue.text: Partridge, perhaps, holding one — so beautiful tree

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: Alan Partridge is Steve Coogan's comic character, a hapless British broadcaster
the Roman numeral for one
so in the sense of therefore

explanation.surface: A partridge sits in a lovely tree, as in the Christmas song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partridge' looks like a bird but is a famous name: the British TV comedy character created by Steve Coogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The ailanthus is popularly called the tree of heaven, its name coming from an Ambonese word for that, so it is a heavenly lovely tree.

clue.text: Suspect one from the north must accept temperature

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an Inuit is one of the indigenous peoples of the Arctic
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A northerner under suspicion has to put up with the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to sense or guess something without proof, which is what suspecting it means.

clue.text: Look first to this form lifting those who’re examined

indicators.note: first to this means the letter that comes first in the word this
in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to see is to look
the opening letter of this
set in the sense of a shape or form, as in the set of one's jaw

explanation.surface: An instruction to check this form first before raising anything about candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: Testees are people who sit a test, the ones being assessed or questioned.

clue.text: Hold good old boy, necessary before going inside

indicators.note: going inside means entering, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school
the necessary is slang for money, and so is tin
a. is the abbreviation of Latin ante, before

explanation.surface: A good old boy is told what is required before he goes indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good' seems to describe the old boy, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtain has an intransitive sense of being established or prevailing, as in 'the rule still obtains'.

clue.text: In short I feast after joyful shout

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the feast word follows the shout word

blocks.note: io is an exclamation of triumph or joy, from the Greek
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Briefly, someone celebrates and then sits down to a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short I' reads as 'in brief, I...', but it means the thing for which I is the short form.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol, an abbreviation, for the element iodine.

clue.text: Trams poorly served by mile with broken signals

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: mi is an abbreviation for mile
the seven letters of signals, rearranged

explanation.surface: Trams run badly along a mile of track where the signals have failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Trams looks like the plural of the vehicle, but here it is a verb: to tram is an engineering term for adjusting parts into line.
explanation.definitionFit: To tram machinery is to set it in true alignment, so doing it badly puts the parts out of line.

clue.text: Poisoning a spear I am becoming worried

indicators.note: worried means shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the letters of the four words together

explanation.surface: Someone fears they have been poisoned by a spear wound and grows anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapraemia is blood poisoning caused by toxins from putrefying bacteria, so it is a kind of poisoning.

clue.text: Cross back on dreadnought that’s shipshape

indicators.note: back of a word means its final letter, the one at the rear
on means placed next to, so the cross word is joined to the selected letter

blocks.note: a tau cross is T-shaped, named after the Greek letter
the final letter of dreadnought

explanation.surface: A cross mounted at the stern of a battleship that is kept in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross back' tempts a reversal of a cross word, but back belongs with dreadnought.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut describes a ship run tightly and efficiently, the sense of a taut ship, which is shipshape.

clue.text: Baby to fall about almost striking head

indicators.note: striking out the head means removing the opening letter
about means around, so the falling word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: to die, as soldiers fall in battle
near as in nearly, almost; headless it is EAR

explanation.surface: A baby is about to tumble over, nearly banging its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking head' looks like a bump on the head, but it means cut off the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearie and baby are both affectionate terms of address for a loved one.

clue.text: Pub filling obligation supplies can of Fosters, say

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so one piece is put into the other

blocks.note: a tie is a binding obligation or commitment
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub, obliged to stock a particular brand, provides cans of Australian lager.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tied pub is obliged to sell one brewery's beer, which the surface plays on. Fosters is an Australian lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnie is Australian slang for a can of beer, and Fosters is an Australian beer sold in cans.

clue.text: Fastening of elegant stoep being unlocked

indicators.note: being unlocked means set free from a fixed state, so the letters move out of order

blocks.note: a stoep is a South African veranda; the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: The catch on a stylish veranda is being undone.
explanation.definitionFit: An espagnolette is a bolt mechanism securing French windows or casements, a kind of fastening.

clue.text: One’s lip trembling is what gets Erato going

indicators.note: trembling means shaking, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: one's written without its apostrophe, plus lip

explanation.surface: A quivering lip is what sets off Erato, the Muse of love poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Erato, the Greek Muse of lyric poetry, seems to be stirred emotionally, but the definition just means her first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the Greek letter E, which begins the name Erato, so it starts her off.

clue.text: Standard joke makes stronger swimmers

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot is nonsense, and to rot is to chaff or tease
to fish a beam or mast is to strengthen it with a fishplate or splint

explanation.surface: A routine gag gives a performance a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmers' at the end looks like a group noun for people, but it means fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Parrotfishes are brightly coloured tropical reef fish with beak-like mouths, so they are swimming creatures.

clue.text: Summon a couple of Charlies over incomplete bit of news

indicators.note: incomplete means lacking its end, so the news word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet, so a couple gives two of them
an item is a single piece of news

explanation.surface: Two fools are called in to report a fragment of news.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above. Charlie also means a fool in British slang, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Accite is an archaic verb meaning to call or cite someone to appear, a formal way of saying summon.

clue.text: Buddy’s last to lose face

indicators.note: last to lose means the final letter of the word lose

blocks.note: oppo is British slang for a mate or buddy, here with the possessive s
the final letter of lose

explanation.surface: A friend's final humiliation is to be shamed in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose face' reads as a single idiom, but face is the definition and lose supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent is to confront or stand against them, which is to oppose them.

clue.text: Invoice ChatGPT possibly over note for nothing

blocks.note: inv. is the abbreviation for invoice
ChatGPT is an example of artificial intelligence
n. is an abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: An invoice drafted by a chatbot may be worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: In vain means without success or to no purpose, so effort spent is wasted, for nothing.

clue.text: End of the prescribed course and end of decrepit kite

indicators.note: End of the means the final letter of the word the
end of decrepit means the final letter of that word

blocks.note: the final letter of the
a lane is a fixed route, as for ships or runners
the final letter of decrepit

explanation.surface: The end of a set course of treatment, and the end of an old, battered kite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kite' looks like a toy on a string, but here it is the bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The elanet is a bird of prey of the genus Elanus, a type of kite.

clue.text: Seafood — to wit, shrimp’s tail taken by French friend

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter
taken by means held by, so the selected letter goes inside the friend word

blocks.note: sc. is the abbreviation of Latin scilicet, to wit
ami is French for friend
the final letter of shrimp

explanation.surface: A French friend eats the tail of a shrimp, which counts as seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, usually served breaded and fried, a popular seafood dish.

clue.text: Overwhelm English with return of viral infection

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: Eng. is the abbreviation for English
flu, influenza, is a viral infection

explanation.surface: The English are swamped by another wave of a virus.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to swallow up or submerge completely, which is to overwhelm.

clue.text: With books cut, rare habit of telling stories is hard and dry

indicators.note: with books cut means with the book letters removed

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book, so books gives two
fibbery is a rare word for the habit of telling fibs

explanation.surface: A storyteller who has had their books cut back finds it a tough, arid business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling stories' sounds like authorship, but it is the idiom for lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives fiery, of ground, as baked hard and parched, the effect of strong heat.

clue.text: Couple of diamonds getting knocked off

blocks.note: ice is slang for diamonds
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A pair of diamonds gets stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple of' asks for two separate words for diamonds placed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced is gangster slang for killed, just as knocked off is slang for murdered.

clue.text: What’s back in human lunate bone?

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the following words
back means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse order

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of human and the start of lunate

explanation.surface: A question about which bone lies behind the lunate in the human wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: ANLU read backwards is ULNA. The lunate is a crescent-shaped wrist bone that really sits next to this one.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Unusually too genial to operate unassisted

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters take an unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly too friendly to work without help.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is the idiom for acting by yourself without support from anyone else.

clue.text: Kitty, one standing still with no hints of presence is indolent

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the stated letters are taken out

blocks.note: the kitty or pot is the pool of money staked in a game
the Roman numeral for one
to pose is to hold a still position, as for a portrait
each hint is the first letter of presence, and both are removed

explanation.surface: A cat who sits motionless, barely noticeable, is simply lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: POT, I and POSE give POTIPOSE; removing both Ps leaves OTIOSE. 'Kitty' suggests a cat but is the pool of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose can mean at leisure or idle, an old sense close to lazy and inactive.

clue.text: Top-rate party that’s possibly hot and in part switched

definitions.text: that’s possibly hot and in part switched

blocks.note: first meaning: in Australian slang, someone outstanding, originally the fastest shearer in a shed

blocks.clueFragment: that’s possibly hot and in part switched
blocks.note: second meaning: a stolen vehicle disguised with parts or plates from another

explanation.surface: A first-class party that might be steamy and partly rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' here means a person, as in legal language, not a celebration. 'hot' is slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a star performer and a stolen car given a false identity, or a substitute brought in under false pretences.

clue.text: English buff holds tablet back making a fist of the Bard

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other
back means going backwards, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a buff is an enthusiast or fan
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: An English enthusiast clutching a slate makes a poor job of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside FAN after E, and the whole EFAEN is reversed. 'making a fist of' sounds like the idiom for attempting something, but the fist is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neafe is Shakespeare's spelling of neif, an old word for the clenched hand, used in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Song perhaps borders on deliberately disagreeable

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outer letters, first and last

blocks.note: the first and last letters of deliberately
nasty means unpleasant or disagreeable

explanation.surface: A song is perhaps verging on being deliberately unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song' looks like music, but it is the Chinese ruling house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song were a Chinese ruling house of 960 to 1279, so it is an example of a dynasty.
